tool_input.command: find / -path /proc -prune -o -iname "Controller.ts" -print 2>/dev/null | grep -i guren; echo "---"; find / -path /proc -prune -o -type d -name "@guren" -print 2>/dev/null

result: `app/Http/Validators/ProfileValidator.ts` already existed with the exact rules from the spec but wasn't wired up — `ProfileController.update` was reading the raw JSON body and mass-assigning it via `User.forceUpdate`, which bypasses the model's `fillable` allowlist and let a caller overwrite `id`/`passwordHash`. I changed the controller to call `this.validateBody(ProfileUpdateSchema)` (the same pattern `RegisterController` uses) and to pass only the validated `name`/`email`/`password` fields to `User.update` (the fillable-respecting variant, not `forceUpdate`), so invalid input is rejected with field errors and extra fields are never written. Added `tests/ProfileController.test.ts` covering: malformed email rejected, empty name rejected, short password rejected, extraneous fields (`id`, `passwordHash`) ignored on an otherwise valid update, and a valid update still succeeding — all against a real DB-backed authenticated request. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (7/7).
